statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-134703: in libexpat 2.10.0 and earlier, the UTF-16 to UTF-16 conversion functions in xmltok.c (DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF16) can split a valid surrogate pair when output space is short, so a crafted document in non-native byte order UTF-16 can deliver a lone high surrogate to the character data and default handlers (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-134703, https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/pull/1519). Only builds compiled with XML_UNICODE convert parser input with those functions; a UTF-8 build converts with XmlUtf8Convert instead (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/blob/R_2_9_0/expat/lib/xmlparse.c). Upstream fixed it after the 2.10.0 release in https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/commit/702389c818cb402f2423fa998fa11907d621959f, which no expat release contains yet, and Debian lists trixie's 2.9.0-1~deb13u1 as vulnerable. The DHI expat packages for Debian 13 are built from Debian's expat 2.7.1, 2.8.2, 2.8.3 and 2.9.0 sources. We unpacked every published build for amd64 and arm64: each libexpat1 package ships both libexpat.so.1, a UTF-8 build, and libexpatw.so.1, an XML_UNICODE build (its feature list names XML_UNICODE, which libexpat.so.1 does not), and each libexpat1-dev package ships the matching static libexpat.a and libexpatw.a. None of these builds carries the fix, so applications that use libexpatw are affected; libexpat.so.1 and the xmlwf program built on it convert input to UTF-8 and do not use the affected functions.
